incidents.cause: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from power lines. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's preoccupation with personal affairs.
An undetermined mechanical malfuction associated with the tail rotor drive system which led to a loss of control.
The loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined based on the available evidence.
A loss of engine power due to fuel starvation as a result of the pilot's failure to follow the pre-landing checklist and verifying the position of the fuel selector.
A failure of the tail rotor pitch change lever assembly due to incorrectly installed bolts and maintenance personnel’s inadequate inspection of the tail rotor control system.
The pilot’s improper response to a simulated engine failure and the instructor’s delayed and improper remedial action.
